questions.prompt: A plugin puts the current time on the first line of the system prompt. What happens to reuse across steps?
options: Nothing changes, because the provider ignores the system prompt
Only the time line is reprocessed
Reuse drops to almost nothing, because the first token differs on every step and everything after it is processed again
Reuse improves because the provider sees fresh data
questions.explanation: Reuse stops at the first differing token. A changing first line means no shared beginning, so the whole request is processed again each step.

questions.prompt: Step 2 sent 4,450 tokens. Step 3 sends those same 4,450 tokens followed by 1,150 new ones. Roughly how many of step 3's tokens can be reused?
options: None, because each request is separate
questions.explanation: Step 3 begins with the whole of step 2, so up to those 4,450 tokens can be reused. The 1,150 new tokens at the end must be processed.

questions.prompt: The system prompt must change in the middle of a session. Which choice keeps the most reuse?
options: Replace the first system message and resend everything
Add a new system message after the existing history
Remove all tools so the request is shorter
questions.explanation: Replacing the first message changes the very start of the request. Adding a new system message at the end keeps the earlier history as an unchanged beginning.
